memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The people of Joseph replied, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the plain have chariots fitted with iron, both those in Beth Shan and its settlements and those in the Valley of Jezreel." But Joshua said to the people of Joseph—to Ephraim and Manasseh—"You are numerous and very powerful. You will have not only one allotment but the forested hill country as well. Clear it, and its farthest limits will be yours; though the Canaanites have chariots fitted with iron and though they are strong, you can drive them out." - Josh 17:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The Joseph tribes push back with their real fear: the Canaanites in the plains have iron chariots. In that age, iron chariots were the most fearsome military technology imaginable — the tanks of the ancient world. The tribes looked at those chariots and concluded the task was impossible. Their eyes were fixed on the strength of the enemy rather than the strength of their God.

Joshua's reply is full of faith. Yes, he acknowledges, the Canaanites have iron chariots and they are strong. He does not deny the difficulty. But he insists: "You can drive them out." Why such confidence? Because the same God who had already given Israel victory after victory was with them still. The iron chariots were real, but they were no match for the Lord. Joshua measured the obstacle against God, not against Israel's fears.

How often we, like these tribes, let the "iron chariots" in our path convince us that God's calling is impossible. The obstacle looms so large that we forget the God who stands with us is larger still. Joshua's words ring out to us too: the difficulty is real, but so is God's power, and in His strength the impossible becomes possible. We do not go forward pretending there are no chariots; we go forward trusting the God for whom no chariot is too strong. Nothing is impossible with Him (Luke 1:37).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "iron chariots" make you feel your challenge is impossible?
- Are you measuring your obstacle against your fears or against God's power?
- How does Joshua's confidence encourage you to move forward in faith?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when the iron chariots in my path make Your calling feel impossible, lift my eyes to You. Remind me that no obstacle is too strong for You, and that with You I can go forward. Amen.
